svg.title: The authority chain: you authorize an agent, the agent acts toward a counterparty, and the action is enforced at a named moment
svg.desc: Diagram of the authority chain. Three boxes in a row: You (the account holder) authorizes the Agent (runs under your name), which acts toward the Counterparty (merchant, platform, registry). Below, four enforcement boxes: Payments at authorization, Purchases at checkout, Platform at the prompt, Extension at the tool call. Two note cards: the audit record is a photograph, not a lock; who answers when the agent acts is still an open question with no operative dispute rule. At the bottom, four responsibility boxes: paired user, account holder, deployer, person who clicked install.

text.tspan: What delegating authorizes — and who answers when it acts
A photograph, not a lock. It documents
what happened — it does not stop a bad
configuration, a mistaken approval, or a dispute.
Who answers when the agent acts: every
document names the human back. An operative
dispute rule has not arrived — forecasts only.
ENFORCED AT A NAMED MOMENT — FOUR SURFACES
EVERY DOCUMENT NAMES A HUMAN BACK
Vendor-documented controls, not independently tested. Terms-of-use layer attributed to trackers, not verified at the page.
